payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD retain recognizable DVD identity?
node.criteria: Pass if the corresponding object is recognizable as a DVD disc or a DVD case from its visible physical form and scene context considered together. A DVD disc need not retain the source case's rectangular outline or printed artwork. Consider circular disc shape, apparent thickness, surface detail and any visible central aperture; an absent or obscured aperture is limited evidence, not by itself proof that DVD identity is lost. Color alone does not establish DVD identity, and a generic circular shape alone is not conclusive. Fail if the counterpart visibly has a non-DVD form lacking recognizable DVD-disc or DVD-case identity, or the target is visibly removed without a corresponding DVD replacement. Unknown if correspondence or the available structural evidence cannot establish whether the counterpart remains recognizable as a DVD.
node.binding: Assess the counterpart of the small printed rectangular DVD item near the source image's center, using the same location and surrounding snow context to establish correspondence even if its outline changes. Inspect whether the central edited white object retains recognizable disc structure, such as a central aperture, or recognizable DVD-case structure. Do not transfer DVD features from the separate white disc on the right to this target. Do not require the original dark coloring or printed artwork to survive the requested whitening.

node_traces.evidence: The corresponding object near the center has changed from the small printed rectangular item to a plain white circular shape. It has no visible central aperture or other clear disc detail, and it does not retain recognizable DVD-case structure. The separate white disc on the right is not the target counterpart.

Tighten the decision node’s evidence-to-label rule so it weighs those cues together and returns unknown when they cannot resolve identity, while preserving the distinction between the target and the right-hand disc. Do not infer that whitening itself means the requested change is absent."}
